facts.statement: The genus Uktenadactylus is an extinct pterosaur from the Early Cretaceous Albian stage of the Paw Paw Formation in Texas, United States.
facts.quote: Uktenadactylus is an extinct genus of anhanguerid pterodactyloid pterosaurs from the Early Cretaceous (Albian stage) Paw Paw Formation of Texas, United States.

facts.statement: The genus contains only one species, Uktenadactylus wadleighi, which is known from a single partial snout fossil originally assigned to the genus Coloborhynchus.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Uktenadactylus wadleighi, known from a single partial snout originally assigned to Coloborhynchus.

facts.statement: The specific name 'wadleighi' honors Chris Wadleigh, the collector of the fossil.
facts.quote: The specific name honors the collector of the fossil, Chris Wadleigh.

facts.statement: In 2009, paleontologists Taissa Rodrigues and Alexander Kellner created the new genus Uktenadactylus for the species C. wadleighi after concluding that the genus Coloborhynchus contained only one species.
facts.quote: In 2009 a study by the Brazilian paleontologists Taissa Rodrigues and Alexander Kellner concluded that Coloborhynchus comprised only a single species, its type species, C. clavirostris. Accordingly, in the same publication they created a new genus for C. wadleighi: Uktenadactylus.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen is a partial snout about fifteen centimetres long, consisting of the premaxilla and a small part of the maxilla.
facts.quote: The holotype and only specimen of U. wadleighi, the partial snout, has a length of about fifteen centimetres and consists of the front end of the skull, containing the premaxilla (cranial bone at the tip of the upper jaw) and a small part of the maxilla (upper jaw).

facts.statement: The fossil preserves the base of a crest that curves upwards to a height of 7.5 cm and a thickness of 4 mm.
facts.quote: On top the base of a crest is present, gradually curving upwards and ending at a height of 7.5 cm, having attained at that point a thickness of 4 mm.

facts.statement: The snout shows eight tooth sockets on the left side and six on the right side.
facts.quote: On the left side eight tooth sockets or alveoli are visible, on the right side six.

facts.statement: The third pair of teeth is the largest, with a diameter of approximately 17.6 to 17.7 mm.
facts.quote: The third pair being the largest with a diameter of either 17.6 mm or 17.7 mm.

facts.statement: Researchers conclude that Uktenadactylus, Coloborhynchus clavirostris, and Siroccopteryx likely formed an unnamed clade within the family Anhangueridae.
facts.quote: The authors conclude from these similarities that the three taxa likely formed an, as yet unnamed, clade together within the Anhangueridae.

facts.statement: Many analyses, including those in 2020, place Uktenadactylus within the family Anhangueridae and the subfamily Coloborhynchinae.
facts.quote: However, many subsequent analyses in the same year as well as in 2020 have recovered Uktenadactylus within the family Anhangueridae, more specifically within the subfamily Coloborhynchinae.

facts.statement: A 2020 analysis by Holgado and Pêgas recovered Uktenadactylus as the sister taxon of Nicorhynchus within the subfamily Coloborhynchinae.
facts.quote: The cladogram on the right is a topology based on the phylogenetic analysis made by Borja Holgado and Rubi Pêgas in 2020, where they recovered Uktenadactylus as the sister taxon of Nicorhynchus within the Coloborhynchinae.

facts.statement: In 2020, a second species, U. rodriguesae, was named based on a snout fragment found on the Isle of Wight.
facts.quote: In 2020, Borja Holgado and Rubi Pêgas named a new species of Uktenadactylus, U. rodriguesae after Rodrigues, known from a snout fragment (cataloged as IWCMS 2014.82) found on the Isle of Wight.

facts.statement: In 2026, the species U. rodriguesae was reassigned to a new genus named Tylodorhynchus.
facts.quote: In 2026, Pêgas and Holgado published a revised description of this species and assigned it to a new genus, Tylodorhynchus.

facts.statement: Uktenadactylus is an extinct pterodactyloid pterosaur genus from the Early Cretaceous found in the Paw Paw Formation of Texas, USA, and the Isle of Wight, southern England.
facts.quote: Uktenadactylus es un género extinto de pterosaurio pterodactiloide del Cretácico Inferior hallado en la formación Paw Paw de Texas, Estados Unidos y Isla de Wight, sur de Inglaterra.

facts.statement: In 2009, Brazilian paleontologists Taissa Rodrigues and Alexander Kellner created the new genus Uktenadactylus for the species C. wadleighi after concluding that Coloborhynchus contained only one species.
facts.quote: En 2009 un estudio hecho por los paleontólogos brasileños Taissa Rodrigues y Alexander Kellner concluyó que Coloborhynchus solo incluía a una especie, su especie tipo C. clavirostris. De acuerdo a esto, en la misma publicación crearon un nuevo género para C. wadleighi: Uktenadactylus.

facts.statement: The genus name derives from Uktena, a horned giant snake from Cherokee mythology, and the Greek term daktylos, meaning "finger," referring to the typical wing finger common in pterosaur names.
facts.quote: El nombre del género se deriva de Uktena, una serpiente gigante con cuerno de la mitología de los Cherokees y el término griego daktylos, "dedo", un elemento común en los nombres de los pterosaurios desde Pterodactylus, refiriéndose a su típico dedo del ala.

facts.statement: The fossil is about fifteen centimeters long and consists of the front end of the skull containing the premaxilla and a small part of the maxilla.
facts.quote: El fósil tiene una longitud de cerca de quince centímetros y consiste en el extremo frontal del cráneo, que contiene el premaxilar y una parte pequeña del maxilar.

facts.statement: A crest on the base curves upward to a height of 7.5 centimeters with a thickness of four millimeters at that point.
facts.quote: Sobre la base hay una cresta que se curva gradualmente hacia arriba y termina en una altura de 7.5 centímetros, habiendo obtenido en este punto un grosor de cuatro milímetros.

facts.statement: Eight tooth sockets are visible on the left side and six on the right side of the fossil.
facts.quote: Sobre el lado izquierdo son visibles ocho alvéolos de los dientes, y sobre el lado derecho seis.

facts.statement: The first pair of teeth was located on the flattened tip of the snout, pointing forward.
facts.quote: El primer par de dientes estaba localizado en la aplanada punta del hocico, apuntando hacia adelante.

facts.statement: The tooth sockets increase in size from the tip backward, with the largest being the third pair having a diameter of 17.6/17.7 millimeters.
facts.quote: Los alvéolos al principio incrementan su tamaño desde la punta hacia atrás, siendo el mayor el tercer par con un diámetro de 17.6/17.7 milímetros.

facts.statement: Rodrigues and Kellner based their distinction between Uktenadactylus and Coloborhynchus clavirostris on stratigraphic, methodological, and phylogenetic considerations.
facts.quote: Rodrigues y Kellner basaron su distinción entre Uktenadactylus y Coloborhynchus clavirostris sobre varias consideraciones estratigráficas, metodológicas y filogenéticas.

facts.statement: Uktenadactylus lived from the Barremian to the Albian stages, between 125.77 and 100.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Albian (125.77 to 100.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: Uktenadactylus belongs to the parent group Coloborhynchinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Coloborhynchinae

facts.statement: Uktenadactylus is classified in the family Anhangueridae.
facts.quote: Family: Anhangueridae

facts.statement: Uktenadactylus is classified as a reptile.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: There is a debate regarding a jaw fragment from the Isle of Wight; while Martill (2015) assigned it to Coloborhynchus, Holgado and Pêgas (2020) described it as a new species of Uktenadactylus, U. rodriguesae.
facts.quote: Martill (2015) describió un fragmento de hocico de la Isla de Wight (IWCMS 2014.82) que asignó a Coloborhynchus. Sin embargo, Holgado y Pêgas (2020) lo encontraron más estrechamente relacionado con Uktendactylus wadleighi y lo describieron como una nueva especie de Uktenadactylus, U. rodriguesae, el nombre específico en honor a Taissa Rodrigues.

rejected.quote: In 1994, Yuong Nam-Lee named a new species within the genus Coloborhynchus: Coloborhynchus wadleighi, based on a partial snout found in 1992 in Albian layers in Tarrant County, holotype SMU 73058 (Shuler Museum of Paleontology, Southern Methodist University at Dallas).
